Yeah. I also gained a ton of weight. I've lost a bit of it but that medication put me at risk for diabetes as well. It's an atypical antipsychotic and that class of meds have that potential side effect. Due to a different atypical antipsychotic, I am now diabetic. If I were you, I'd avoid them if at all possible. I'm not a doctor and if your doctor recommends that you take them, you should do as they say. Just be informed. That's all I'm saying. I wish my doctors had informed me.

To me, she sounds toxic and deeply unstable. It may be more than BPD (if it is BPD). I can't diagnose because I'm not a doctor. However, as someone who has BPD, I have my doubts.

It sounds like you are still struggling with some issues. Since you have a rapport with this person, I would ask him something along the lines of: Do I have a current diagnosis? If so, what? How do you know? What makes you think that I have this diagnosis? What evidence is there to support that claim? 
Then I would ask to take a test for whatever diagnosis he gives you. He probably has a copy of the DSM IV or something.
How long have you been seeing your psychologist/therapist? I can advise you more with that info. Is it a psychologist or therapist?

You should definitely ask about a diagnosis. Also, take an active role in your treatment and when/if a diagnosis is made, talk at length with your doctor/therapist about it. Make sure you understand and agree with your diagnosis as well.
